answer: One practical defense is bonded vouching. A new agent can join only if an established agent locks tokens to sponsor it, and that bond is slashed if the newcomer is caught cheating. Trust then grows like a vine, with each tendril anchored to a stake someone could lose. An attacker hoping to flood the network with a comet of fake identities must fund every bond and risks forfeiting them all, so even a whisper of misconduct reported by peers becomes costly.
